help.introEn: A radio interview of about three minutes with Rafael, an electrician from Spain who came to Germany six years ago because there was no work at home, and who today runs his own business in Nürnberg. He tells what almost drove him back (the language, the bureaucracy, the weather), what kept him and what he advises other skilled workers. The person is invented; the figures on the skills shortage and the recognition of qualifications are real. In language terms you hear what you practised last: the connectors falls, da and trotzdem (Falls es nicht klappt, gehe ich zurück. Da ich die Sprache nicht konnte, …; Trotzdem bin ich geblieben) and the es expressions (es gibt, es geht um, es lohnt sich, es fällt mir schwer, es kommt darauf an). The questions test reasons, consequences and advice.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Since there was no work in Spain, I left; if it had not worked out here, I would have gone back.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The first two years were hard. Nevertheless I never seriously thought of going back.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Contrast between two main clauses: trotzdem, verb right after.
help.tips[0].en.title: falls, da, trotzdem
help.tips[0].en.text: falls = if, for a possible condition (Falls es nicht klappt, gehe ich zurück; subordinate clause, verb at the end). da = since / because, a little more formal, often at the start (Da ich kein Deutsch konnte, bekam ich keine Stelle). trotzdem = nevertheless, a main-clause connector in position 1, verb after it (Es war schwer. Trotzdem bin ich geblieben). Compare: obwohl + subordinate clause (Obwohl es schwer war, bin ich geblieben) says the same as trotzdem + main clause.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: It is not only about money; it is about whether you feel at home here.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: It was worth taking the exam, although I found it hard.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Es kommt darauf an, ob … = it depends on whether ….
help.tips[1].en.title: es expressions
help.tips[1].en.text: es gibt + accusative (Es gibt zu wenige Elektriker), es geht um (Es geht um die Anerkennung meines Abschlusses), es lohnt sich (Es lohnt sich, Deutsch zu lernen), es fällt mir schwer / leicht (Es fiel mir schwer, zu telefonieren), es kommt darauf an (Es kommt darauf an, wo man wohnt), es tut mir leid, es macht nichts, es hängt davon ab, es ist mir egal, wie geht es dir. The es always stays; with weather and time (es regnet, es ist spät) it is similarly fixed.
help.rememberEn[0]: falls (if), da (since) + subordinate clause; trotzdem + main clause with the verb in position 2.
help.rememberEn[1]: es gibt, es geht um, es lohnt sich, es fällt mir schwer, es kommt darauf an, es hängt davon ab.
help.examEn: Interviews in which someone tells their story and gives reasons and advice are a typical listening text in the B1 exam.
help.hookEn: No German, no papers, one suitcase to Nürnberg, and six years later his own business. Hear what almost drove Rafael back and why he stayed anyway.
